solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Tailless hatchling is elegant

indicators.note: without its tail, the word for the young bird loses its final letter

parts.note: a newly hatched bird is a chick

explanation.surface: A baby bird with no tail somehow still looks stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a borrowed French word for stylish and fashionable in appearance.

clue.text: Valuable prisoner putting label in socks

indicators.note: the word for a label is placed in the middle of the word for socks

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
a tag is a label

explanation.surface: Someone sewing name tags into a captive's socks.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a captive held as security, prized because of what can be demanded for release.

clue.text: Caught by part of chain in prison

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
a chain is made of links

explanation.surface: A captured criminal is chained up in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Clink is British slang for a jail, possibly from a historic Southwark gaol of that name.

clue.text: Perhaps baron's biography: look closely

parts.note: a biography is a written life of someone
to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A nobleman's memoir that rewards careful reading.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a life peer is a member of the House of Lords whose title, often baron, cannot be inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is one example of a peerage title held for life only, hence 'Perhaps'.

clue.text: Heartfelt request to abolish parking in meadow

indicators.note: abolishing the parking symbol means taking that letter out of the request

parts.note: a plea is an earnest appeal
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A passionate campaign to ban parking on a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea is a poetic word for grassland or pasture.

clue.text: Bird, poor flier — deaf

indicators.note: a poor version of these words is a badly arranged one, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Describing a bird that flies badly and cannot hear.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush that winters in Britain.

clue.text: I see doctor: obvious I must be admitted

indicators.note: the second I is taken into the word for obvious, as a hospital admits someone

parts.note: patent means plainly evident

explanation.surface: Someone frankly confessing that they are seeing a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sees a doctor for treatment is that doctor's case, the person under medical care.

clue.text: Call up woman to receive approval

indicators.note: the woman's name takes in the word for approval

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis
OK signals approval

explanation.surface: Phoning a woman to get her sign-off.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to summon a memory or feeling, as to call up a past scene.

clue.text: Like illegal broadcaster to pronounce his aitches

parts.note: as means in the manner of
a pirate radio station broadcasts without a licence

explanation.surface: A pirate DJ proud of saying every H.
explanation.walkthrough: Pirate radio stations, broadcasting from ships off the British coast in the 1960s, were famously unlicensed.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetically, sounding the breathy H at the start of a word is exactly this.

clue.text: Implement return of robbery proceeds

indicators.note: the stolen goods word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: loot is stolen goods

explanation.surface: Carrying out the handing back of stolen money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implement' reads as a verb but defines a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a tool or utensil for doing work.

clue.text: Cover up mother's knee at first

parts.note: ma is mother, plus the S from the possessive

indicators.note: only the opening letter of knee is used

explanation.surface: Hiding a mother's knee under a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: To mask something is to conceal or disguise it.

clue.text: Again considered to be recovered

parts.note: re- is a prefix meaning again
deemed means judged or considered

explanation.surface: Something reconsidered and found to be mended.
explanation.definitionFit: Redeemed can mean bought back or regained, as with a pawned item.

clue.text: Distasteful ruling about turning up

indicators.note: the word for ruling goes around the other piece

parts.note: regnant means reigning, as in queen regnant

indicators.note: the little word up is turned around

explanation.surface: An unpleasant regulation on showing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant means offensive or repellent.

clue.text: Abscond from city in moist air

indicators.note: the city's postcode sits inside the word for moist air

parts.note: damp is moisture in the air
EC is the postcode area for the City of London

explanation.surface: Fleeing the humid atmosphere of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly or secretly, to run away.

clue.text: A mature eccentric, doing it for love?

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd older person doing something just for the joy of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin amator means lover, so an unpaid enthusiast does it for love.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-professional pursues a pastime for its own sake rather than money.

clue.text: Criticise a sailor's course in sound

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, giving letters that sound the same

parts.note: a tack is a course sailed on one side of the wind

explanation.surface: Finding fault with a yachtsman's route through a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a sea channel, the sailor's water, but signals that 'a tack' is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To attack is to criticise strongly, a verbal assault.

clue.text: Warship offering free curries

indicators.note: the letters are set free to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A navy vessel serving complimentary curries.
explanation.definitionFit: A cruiser is a fast, medium-sized naval fighting vessel.

clue.text: Earn a hug, changing angry speech

indicators.note: changing these words means altering the order of their letters

explanation.surface: Winning an embrace by toning down an angry tirade.
explanation.definitionFit: A harangue is a long, aggressive lecture or rant.

clue.text: Volunteers to hold up a gold vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue the volunteers sit beneath, supporting the other pieces

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
the TA, Territorial Army, is Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers staging a robbery for gold aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship but means a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood from the heart, a blood vessel.

clue.text: Sad as some music is cut short

indicators.note: the music word loses its final letter

parts.note: the blues is a musical genre

explanation.surface: Feeling down as a melody is interrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue is feeling melancholy or downcast.

clue.text: Suddenly run right into chest

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right goes inside the word for chest

parts.note: bust means chest

explanation.surface: Charging straight into a treasure chest.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst out or burst into a room is to dash or rush suddenly.

clue.text: Time to regret being honest

parts.note: to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Time to be sorry for having been candid.
explanation.definitionFit: Being true means being faithful, sincere and truthful.

clue.text: Daisy is first to kiss star

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like flower

indicators.note: only the opening letter of kiss is wanted

explanation.surface: A girl named Daisy is the first to kiss a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' reads as a name but is a flower; 'star' is the printed symbol, not a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped typographical symbol.

clue.text: Part of body regularly stroked

indicators.note: taking every other letter, at regular intervals, from the word stroked

explanation.surface: A part of someone that is stroked routinely.
explanation.definitionFit: A digit of the foot is one small piece of the human frame.

clue.text: Surrealist friend conceals tough character

indicators.note: the word for friend hides the other word inside it

parts.note: mate is a friend
grit is toughness of character

explanation.surface: A pal of a surrealist painter hiding a hard man.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was the Belgian painter famous for surrealist images like the bowler-hatted man.

clue.text: Aquatic bird's back, not head

indicators.note: the word for back loses its first letter

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: Describing a water bird's back but not its head.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay; 'back' is the rear of a boat, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender seabirds related to gulls.
